title: Time Zone Converter: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Time Zone Converter: Convert a specific local date and time between world timezones with daylight-saving rules applied. Learn how to use it, the formula…
content:
The [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert a specific local date and time between world timezones with daylight-saving rules applied. Enter your date in source timezone, local time (24-hour), from timezone and to timezone and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A timezone conversion maps one exact instant to local clocks in different places. Unlike adding a fixed number of hours, this converter uses the browser's IANA timezone database, including daylight-saving transitions and regional offsets for the selected date. That distinction matters for international meetings, travel, broadcasts and deadlines near seasonal clock changes. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Time Zone Converter

Start by picking your date in source timezone, then typing or pasting your local time (24-hour), choosing your from timezone from the list and finally choosing your to timezone from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the date and 24-hour wall-clock time as observed in the source timezone.
2. Choose the source city or region, then the destination timezone.
3. Check the converted full date as well as the clock time; crossing midnight can move the meeting to another day.

## Formula

The source wall time is resolved to a UTC instant using the source region's offset on that date, then formatted with the destination region's offset at the same instant. No fixed hour difference is assumed.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 12:00 in New York on 14 November 2026 is 17:00 UTC. In Karachi, which is UTC+5 on that date, it is 22:00 on the same calendar day. Try the same figures in the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Date in source timezone: 2026-11-14, Local time (24-hour): 12:00, From timezone: New York (US Eastern), To timezone: Karachi), the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) returns Converted local time: 22:00 GMT+5, Full converted date and time: Saturday, November 14, 2026 at 10:00:00 PM GMT+5, Source time: Nov 14, 2026, 12:00 PM, Exact UTC instant: 2026-11-14T17:00:00Z, Destination timezone: Asia/Karachi. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Age Calculator](/age-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Why city timezones are better than fixed abbreviations

Labels such as EST and CST can be ambiguous and do not describe every seasonal rule. IANA regions such as America/New_York apply daylight saving on the correct dates, while Asia/Karachi and Asia/Kolkata use their own current and historical rules. Always share the date when arranging a conversion because offsets can change during the year.

## Clock-change gaps and repeated times

When clocks move forward, some local times do not exist; when they move back, a local time can occur twice. The converter resolves entries through the environment's timezone rules, but for critical events in those windows, confirm the offset or UTC instant with every participant. Use the displayed ISO UTC value as an unambiguous reference.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Include the full date in every international invitation.
- Use the UTC instant to remove ambiguity around daylight-saving transitions.
- Confirm unusual historical offsets with an authoritative timezone record when working with archival data.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does this account for daylight saving time?

Yes. It uses IANA regional timezone data for the selected date rather than a fixed offset, including daylight-saving rules supported by the browser. Try it with your own numbers in the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does the converted date sometimes change?

Timezones can be many hours apart. A source time near midnight can fall on the previous or next calendar day at the destination. Try it with your own numbers in the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What does the Z in the UTC result mean?

Z indicates Coordinated Universal Time with zero offset. The ISO timestamp identifies the same exact instant independent of local clock conventions. Try it with your own numbers in the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Time Zone Converter use?

The source wall time is resolved to a UTC instant using the source region's offset on that date, then formatted with the destination region's offset at the same instant. No fixed hour difference is assumed. You can see it in action in the [Time Zone Converter](/time-zone-converter) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Time Zone Converter?

Just Date in source timezone, Local time (24-hour), From timezone and To timezone. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
